doc.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995

title: His debut big band CD and Milestone, Bob Weinstock
summary: Duffy talks about his debut CD, the young players on it, and Milestone/Fantasy with Bob Weinstock producing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, I have to compliment you — this is a great piece of work.
Thank you, Monk. This is my debut CD. I hope everyone enjoys it.
And I’m wondering where all these young players come from — there is some hot stuff on here.
A lot of these guys are wonderful musicians, you know? I owe them a lot of money at this point, but that’s—they’re still friendly.
Yeah. They won’t forget about it.
The most important thing is they gave me an opportunity to musically expose them to the world, you know. Because Milestone Fantasy has been very kind to help promote my

career at the moment, and Mr. Bob Weinstock, who used to, who started Prestige Records, he’s graciously come out of semi-retirement down in Florida to produce some records for Milestone now, and I’m very, very honored and thrilled that I could be part of his, you know, return into the industry.
